mainTopic: Gifts and a כתובה as signs of קידושין, and simultaneous קידושין of two sisters
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה. If a man's first קידושין failed, because he gave less than a פרוטה or because he was a קטן, gifts he sends later do not make her מקודשת. The גמרא explains why each case had to be listed. רב הונא and רבה rule that in general we worry gifts were sent as קידושין. The גמרא gives two versions of how our משנה fits with that rule, and רב פפא settles it: it depends on whether the local custom is to send gifts before or after קידושין. The same pattern is applied to a כתובה seen in public, and רב אשי ties that case to local custom too. A new משנה then teaches that קידושין to a woman and her sister (or her daughter) in one act works for neither of them. רבא explains this with רבה's rule: what cannot take effect one after the other cannot take effect at the same time. אביי begins a challenge to that rule, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Later gifts do not create betrothal after a failed first betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by ruling that the woman is not מקודשת, even though he sent gifts afterward. He sent them because of the first, invalid קידושין, and the same applies to a קטן who was מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: She is not betrothed, because he sent the gifts on account of the first betrothal. And the same is true of a minor who betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the משנה. It says that gifts sent after a failed קידושין do not count as a new קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier cases in the משנה (just before this line) were a man who betrothed two women with one פרוטה, or one woman with less than a פרוטה. The reason she stays unmarried is his intent: he thought the first קידושין worked, so the gifts were just gifts. The משנה adds a קטן to the list: if he sends gifts after growing up, they are also because of his old, invalid קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: The first betrothal (the one that did not work)
A minor, a boy under בר מצוה

phrases.english: she is not betrothed,
because he sent [the gifts] on account of the first betrothal.
And the same applies to a minor who betrothed.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gifts sent after an invalid קידושין (less than a פרוטה, or by a קטן) do not create קידושין, because they were sent on account of the first attempt.

steps.title: Why the less-than-a-פרוטה case is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a צריכותא. If the משנה had only taught the case of one פרוטה for two women, we might think the case of less than a פרוטה for one woman is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And it is necessary to list each case. If the משנה had only taught the case of one פרוטה, we would say he made a mistake because real money left his hands. But with less than a פרוטה, I might say he knows that betrothal does not work with less than a פרוטה, so when he sends gifts, he sends them to betroth her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה had to list the less-than-a-פרוטה case and could not stop at the one-פרוטה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the one-פרוטה case, a full פרוטה really left his pocket, so it makes sense that he thought he was already married. When he gave less than a פרוטה, we might assume he knew it was worthless, so his later gifts were a fresh attempt at קידושין. The משנה teaches that even here, the gifts do not count.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary. This opens an explanation of why each case is listed.
Worth a פרוטה, the minimum value for קידושין
Gifts a groom sends to his bride

steps.confusionAlert: The 'שווה פרוטה' case is not a valid קידושין. It is one פרוטה split between two women, so each woman gets less than a פרוטה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And it is necessary,
for if it had taught us [only the case of] worth a peruta,
phrases.notes: This is the case where he betrothed two women with one פרוטה together.

phrases.aramaic: אַיְּידֵי דְּקָא נָפֵיק מָמוֹנָא מִינֵּיהּ – טָעֵי,
phrases.english: since money went out from him, he errs,
but [with] less than a peruta's worth,
I might say he knows that betrothal does not take effect
with less than a peruta's worth
and when he sends gifts,
he sends them with the intention of betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה needed the less-than-a-פרוטה case in addition to the one-פרוטה case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The less-than-a-פרוטה case is needed, because there we might have thought he knew his first קידושין failed and sent the gifts as a new קידושין.

steps.title: Why the minor's case is also needed
steps.stepSummary: The צריכותא continues. Even with both פרוטה cases, the קטן case is needed, because everyone knows a קטן's קידושין means nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us only these two cases, I would say that is because people do not clearly know the difference between a פרוטה and less than a פרוטה. But a minor who betrothed: everyone knows a minor's betrothal is nothing. So I might say that when he sends gifts, he sends them for betrothal. That is why the משנה teaches us this case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why the משנה also had to mention a קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פרוטה cases, the man might honestly be confused about the money rules, so he thought he was already married. With a קטן, everyone knows his קידושין is worthless, so we might think his later gifts were surely meant as a real קידושין. The משנה teaches that even here we say he sent them because of the first attempt.

keyTerms.meaning: People are not clear about it
It teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: Each case in the משנה adds a new חידוש. Even where the man seemingly should have known his first קידושין failed, we still assume his later gifts were sent because of that first attempt.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us these two,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּבֵין פְּרוּטָה לְפָחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
phrases.english: [I would say it is] because between a peruta and less than a peruta's worth
people are not clear.
phrases.notes: Since people mix up these money rules, the man likely thought he was already married.

phrases.english: But a minor who betrothed,

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל יוֹדְעִין שֶׁאֵין קִידּוּשֵׁי קָטָן כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: everyone knows that a minor's betrothal is nothing,
I might say: when he sends gifts,
he sends them with the intention of betrothal,
[so] it teaches us [otherwise].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכותא, moving from the two פרוטה cases to the קטן case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three cases are needed. Even for a קטן, whose קידושין everyone knows is worthless, later gifts are assumed to be sent because of the first attempt.

steps.title: רב הונא and רבה: we worry about gifts
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רבה both rule חוששין לסבלונות: we must worry that gifts a man sends to a woman may have been meant as קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב הונא says: We worry about gifts. And רבה said the same: We worry about gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of אמוראים. When a man sends a woman gifts, we must be concerned that this might be a קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a general rule, separate from the משנה's special cases. Because of this worry, the woman may need a גט before she marries someone else. This ruling sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. This introduces a statement of אמוראים.
We are concerned; we take the possibility into account

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical concern for halacha: gifts can create a doubtful קידושין.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav Huna said:
We are concerned about gifts.
phrases.notes: He means we worry the gifts may have been sent as קידושין.

phrases.english: And so said Rabba:
We are concerned about gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְסִבְלוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה to a general ruling about gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We must worry that gifts sent to a woman might be קידושין.

steps.title: רבה's challenge from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה reports that they challenged their own ruling from the משנה, which says that even after gifts were sent, she is not מקודשת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: And we raised a challenge against our ruling: 'Even if he sent gifts afterward, she is not betrothed!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a challenge against the rule 'we worry about gifts.' The משנה seems to say gifts do not create קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gifts were a reason to worry about קידושין, the משנה should not say flatly that she is not מקודשת after gifts were sent. So the משנה seems to go against חוששין לסבלונות.

phrases.english: Rabba said: And we raised an objection against our ruling:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשָּׁלַח סִבְלוֹנוֹת לְאַחַר מִכָּאן –
phrases.english: Even though he sent gifts afterward,
she is not betrothed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 4 using the משנה from step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that gifts do not create קידושין, which seems to go against worrying about gifts.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה gives its own reason
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה is a special case. It says why she is not מקודשת: the gifts were sent because of the first קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: There, the reason is as the משנה itself teaches: because he sent them on account of the first betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבה's challenge. The משנה is different because there was an earlier failed קידושין that explains why the gifts were sent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the gifts have an obvious reason: he thought he was already married. Where there was no earlier קידושין, there is no such explanation, so the gifts could be meant as קידושין, and we still worry. The משנה is an exception and does not cancel the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is as it is taught

steps.whatToRemember: חוששין לסבלונות stays in force. The משנה is a special case, because the gifts there are explained by the earlier failed קידושין.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
There, the reason is as it teaches:
because he sent [them] on account of the first betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הָתָם כִּדְקָתָנֵי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the משנה has a special reason that does not apply elsewhere.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that gifts never create a concern of קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only where an earlier failed קידושין explains the gifts do we say they are not קידושין. Otherwise we still worry about gifts.

steps.title: Second version: רבה proves his rule from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: In this second version, רבה says the משנה supports him. Because the משנה gives a special reason why she is not מקודשת, in a normal case the gifts would count as קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some tell it differently. רבה said: How do I know my rule? The משנה gives a reason: he sent the gifts because of the first קידושין. So only here, where he made a mistake, is there no קידושין. But in a normal case, the gifts are קידושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the story. In this version the same משנה that was used against רבה becomes רבה's own proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (Steps 5-6), the משנה was a challenge to רבה and אביי had to answer it. Here רבה reads the משנה's reason as a limit. The man only failed to make קידושין because he wrongly thought he was already married to her. Take away that mistake, and the gifts would count as קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of the discussion
From where do I say it? (How do I know this?)
In general, in an ordinary case

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first version the משנה was a קשיא against רבה. In this version רבה uses the very same משנה as his proof.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rabba said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is his rule that we worry gifts may be קידושין.

phrases.english: Since the Mishna teaches a reason:
Because he sent them on account of the first betrothal.
It is here that he made a mistake.
phrases.notes: He wrongly thought the first, failed קידושין had worked, so he never meant the gifts as new קידושין.

phrases.english: But in general, they are a betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אָמַר רַבָּה: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells Steps 5-6 differently. The משנה becomes a proof for רבה instead of a challenge to him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's stated reason: 'שמחמת קידושין הראשונים שלח' suggests that without that mistake, gifts would be קידושין

steps.title: אביי rejects the proof: the משנה teaches 'not only, but even'
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה is teaching a bigger point. In a normal case, of course gifts are not קידושין. The משנה teaches that even here, where he already started with קידושין, the gifts still don't count.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? He says the משנה is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that in an ordinary case, where he never started any קידושין, the gifts are not קידושין. But even here, where he did start a קידושין, you might think the gifts count as קידושין. So the משנה teaches us that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבה's proof by reading the משנה the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה read the משנה as: 'only here is it not קידושין.' אביי reads it as: 'even here it is not קידושין, and surely not in a normal case.' The case in the משנה is actually the stronger case for קידושין, because he already had קידושין on his mind. So the משנה proves nothing for רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary (to say): a 'not only this, but even that' style
He entered into the framework of קידושין (he already started the process)
I might say / you might have thought

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the same line in a משנה can be read as a limit ('only here') or as a stronger case ('even here'). The whole proof depends on which reading you choose.

phrases.english: And Abaye? It is speaking in the style of 'it is not necessary.'
phrases.notes: Meaning: how does אביי deal with רבה's proof? He reads the משנה as 'not only, but even.'

phrases.english: It is not necessary to say this in an ordinary case,
where he did not enter into the matter of betrothal at all,
but even here,
where he did enter into the matter of betrothal
I might say: they are a betrothal,
so it teaches us that they are not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's proof from Step 7 by reading the משנה as 'even here' instead of 'only here.'
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה. It does not decide the law itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה assumed the משנה's reason limits the ruling to this case. But it may be a 'לא מיבעיא' style, teaching the harder case.

steps.title: So what is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final law is about gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: What came of it? (What is the final ruling?)
steps.whatsHappening: After the back-and-forth, the גמרא asks for the bottom line: do we worry about סבלונות or not? This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither version settled the matter. In the first version the challenge from the משנה was answered, and in the second version רבה's proof was rejected. So the גמרא asks directly for the practical law.

keyTerms.meaning: What came of it? (What is the final conclusion?)

phrases.english: What came of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate over proofs to asking for the final law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical ruling: do we worry that gifts were meant as קידושין?

steps.title: רב פפא: it depends on the local custom
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules: where the custom is to do קידושין first and then send gifts, we worry. Where the custom is to send gifts first and then do קידושין, we don't worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In a place where people first do קידושין and afterward send gifts, we worry. In a place where people first send gifts and afterward do קידושין, we don't worry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the final ruling, and it depends on how people in that place usually act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gifts normally come only after קידושין, then seeing gifts suggests a קידושין already happened, so we must worry she is מקודשת. If gifts normally come before קידושין, gifts tell us nothing, so there is no worry.

keyTerms.meaning: A place (a town with its own custom)

steps.whatToRemember: The final law on סבלונות depends on local custom. If gifts usually come after קידושין, we worry she is מקודשת. If they usually come before, we don't.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In a place where they betroth and afterward send gifts,
we are concerned;
phrases.notes: We worry she is already מקודשת, since gifts there normally come after קידושין.

phrases.english: where they send gifts and afterward betroth, we are not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּאַתְרָא דִּמְקַדְּשִׁי וַהֲדַר מְסַבְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9 with a practical ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It depends on custom: where קידושין comes before gifts, we worry; where gifts come first, we don't.

steps.title: Isn't the first case obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: if everyone there does קידושין before gifts, isn't it obvious that gifts mean קידושין happened?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they do קידושין first and then send gifts, that's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב פפא needed to say the first half of his ruling at all, since it seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If gifts are only ever sent after קידושין in that place, then of course gifts point to קידושין. So the גמרא asks what new point רב פפא is teaching.

phrases.english: Where they betroth and afterward send gifts, it is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the first half of רב פפא's ruling teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's first case: באתרא דמקדשי והדר מסבלי חיישינן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the custom is clear, the ruling seems too obvious to need saying.

steps.title: Needed for a place with a majority and a minority custom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב פפא means a mixed place: most people do קידושין first, but some send gifts first. We follow the majority and still worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for a place where most people do קידושין first and then send gifts, and a minority send gifts first and then do קידושין. You might think we should take the minority into account. So רב פפא teaches us that we don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point in רב פפא's ruling: it is about a town where people don't all follow the same custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a mixed town, this man might belong to the minority who send gifts before קידושין, and then the gifts would prove nothing. רב פפא teaches that we ignore the minority. We follow the majority custom, so we still worry she is מקודשת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this specific case)
You might have said / you might think
Let us take into account / be concerned about

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's ruling applies even in a mixed town. We follow the majority custom (קידושין first, then gifts), so we still worry that the gifts mean she is מקודשת.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where most betroth and afterward send gifts,
and a minority send gifts and afterward betroth.
You might have said: let us take the minority into account,
phrases.notes: Then we would think these gifts might have come before any קידושין, so there is nothing to worry about.

phrases.english: so it teaches us that we do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּרוּבָּא מְקַדְּשִׁי וַהֲדַר מְסַבְּלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'פשיטא' challenge of Step 11 by narrowing רב פפא's case to a mixed-custom place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a place with a majority and a minority custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might take the minority custom into account and not worry about קידושין.
steps.terutzMaskana: We follow the majority custom and do worry about קידושין.

steps.title: Does a marriage contract seen in public show she is married?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב הונא asks רבא whether a כתובה seen in the marketplace makes us treat a woman as married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב הונא asked רבא: If a woman's marriage contract became known in the marketplace, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins, related to the gifts discussion. Someone asks whether a כתובה with a woman's name, seen in public, means we must treat her as an אשת איש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gifts were one possible sign of קידושין. A כתובה is a stronger-looking sign, since it is a real marriage document. The question is whether that is enough to assume קידושין already happened.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a formal question to a teacher)

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא מֵרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Huna asked Rava:
If a marriage contract became known in the marketplace, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא מֵרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from gifts to a different public sign of marriage: a כתובה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a publicly seen כתובה makes a woman a ספק אשת איש.

steps.title: רבא: a marriage contract alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a כתובה seen in public is not a reason to treat her as married.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: And just because a marriage contract became known in the marketplace, should we treat her as a married woman?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers with a question that means "of course not". A כתובה being out there does not make her an אשת איש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כתובה is only a document. A man can write it before any קידושין, even without the woman knowing. So the paper alone does not prove a marriage happened.

keyTerms.meaning: And should...? (a question that expects the answer "no")

phrases.english: He said to him:
And just because there became known
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, but the corrected wording is the one in square brackets, "became known."

phrases.english: a marriage contract in the marketplace
should we treat her as a married woman?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּחְזַק שְׁטַר כְּתוּבָּה בַּשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כתובה in public does not on its own make her a married woman.

steps.title: What is the final law about the marriage contract?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the final ruling on the כתובה case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the bottom-line law about a public כתובה, the same way it did with gifts in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gave a general answer, but the גמרא wants a practical ruling. This sets up רב אשי's ruling, which looks a lot like רב פפא's ruling about gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: What was concluded about it? (asking for the final law)

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the final law after רבא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical final ruling about a publicly seen כתובה.

steps.title: רב אשי: it depends on local custom
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules: where they do קידושין first and then write the כתובה, we worry. Where they write first and then do קידושין, we don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: In a place where they betroth first and afterward write the marriage contract, we are concerned. Where they write first and afterward betroth, we are not concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the final law. It follows the local custom of what comes first, the קידושין or the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the custom is קידושין first, then a written כתובה suggests קידושין already happened, so we worry. If the custom is כתובה first, a כתובה proves nothing. This is the same pattern as רב פפא's rule about gifts in step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned (that she may be married)

steps.whatToRemember: A כתובה, like gifts, counts as a sign of קידושין only where the local order is קידושין first.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
In a place where they betroth first
and afterward write the marriage contract, we are concerned;
where they write and afterward betroth, we are not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי בְּאַתְרָא דִּמְקַדְּשִׁי וַהֲדַר כָּתְבִי כְּתוּבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for the final law.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Worry only where the custom is קידושין before the כתובה.

steps.title: Isn't the first case obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: where they always do קידושין first, it is obvious that a כתובה means קידושין happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they betroth and then write, that's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. It says the first half of his ruling is too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone there writes the כתובה only after קידושין, then a כתובה clearly points to קידושין. So why did רב אשי have to teach it?

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a ruling teaches nothing new)

phrases.english: Where they betroth and then write, that's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of רב אשי's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's ruling that we worry where קידושין comes before the כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems self-evident, so there is no reason to state it.

steps.title: Needed where a scribe is rare
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed where scribes are rare. We might think he wrote the כתובה early only because a scribe happened to be there, so רב אשי teaches that we still worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where a scribe isn't commonly around. You might have said that it was just that a scribe happened to come by, so he wrote it early. So it teaches us that we still worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב אשי's ruling teaches something new in a special case: a place where scribes are hard to find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There, we might think the man used a passing scribe to write the כתובה early, before קידושין. רב אשי teaches that we don't assume this. We still follow the local custom and worry that קידושין happened.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a special case)

steps.whatToRemember: Even a reasonable excuse for an early כתובה does not override the local custom of קידושין first.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where a scribe isn't commonly around.
You might have said
it was just that a scribe happened to come by,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ruling to a specific case where it teaches something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Where scribes are rare, an early כתובה may only mean a scribe happened by, so we would not worry.
steps.terutzMaskana: We still follow the custom of קידושין first and worry.

steps.title: משנה: betrothing two close relatives at once fails
steps.stepSummary: If a man does קידושין to a woman and her daughter, or a woman and her sister, at the same moment, neither is betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who betroths a woman and her daughter, or a woman and her sister, at one time, they are not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that קידושין to two women who are forbidden to be married together, done in one act, does not work for either of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He cannot be married to both, since they are relatives forbidden together. Since neither woman comes before the other, there is no reason to pick one. So the קידושין fails for both.

keyTerms.meaning: At one time, in a single act

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who betroths a woman and her daughter
or a woman and her sister at one time,
they are not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ אִשָּׁה וּבִתָּהּ אוֹ אִשָּׁה וַאֲחוֹתָהּ כְּאַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Simultaneous קידושין to two women forbidden together takes effect for neither.

steps.title: The story of five women and a basket of figs
steps.stepSummary: A man betrothed five women, including two sisters, with one basket of figs. The חכמים ruled that the sisters were not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident with five women, and two of them were sisters. A man gathered a basket of figs. The figs were theirs, and they were from the seventh year. He said: "You are all betrothed to me with this basket," and one woman accepted it for all of them. The חכמים said: The sisters are not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a real story that shows its rule in action. The two sisters were betrothed together in one act, so their קידושין did not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story adds a case with more than two women: only the sisters are named as not betrothed. The details about the figs are told here, but the משנה gives no ruling on them.

keyTerms.meaning: On behalf of all of them

phrases.english: And there was an incident with five women
and among them were two sisters,

phrases.aramaic: וְלִיקֵּט אָדָם אֶחָד כַּלְכַּלָּה שֶׁל תְּאֵנִים.
phrases.english: and one man gathered a basket of figs.
And it was theirs, and it was from the seventh year,
phrases.notes: "Theirs" means the figs came from the women's own field.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר: ״הֲרֵי כּוּלְּכֶם מְקוּדָּשׁוֹת לִי בְּכַלְכַּלָּה זוֹ״,
phrases.english: and he said: "You are all betrothed to me with this basket,"

phrases.aramaic: וְקִיבְּלָה אַחַת מֵהֶן עַל יְדֵי כּוּלָּן.
phrases.english: and one of them accepted it on behalf of all of them.
And the Sages said: The sisters are not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּחָמֵשׁ נָשִׁים וּבָהֶן שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the משנה's rule with a real incident.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sisters betrothed together in one act are not betrothed.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that קידושין to two sisters at once fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up רמי בר חמא's answer from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think he should at least be betrothed to one of them. The גמרא wants to know what source teaches that neither becomes betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we know these things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that simultaneous קידושין to two sisters fails for both.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא learns it from the word "rivals"
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא reads the פסוק "do not take a woman to her sister, to make them rivals" as saying: when they would become rivals together, he cannot take even one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: For the פסוק says: "Do not take a woman to her sister, to make them rivals." The Torah said: at the moment they would become rival wives to each other, he cannot take even one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא gives the source. He reads the פסוק as being about a single act of קידושין that would make the two sisters rivals at the same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לצרור, "to make rivals", describes both sisters becoming co-wives at once. רמי בר חמא learns that in that case "taking" (קידושין) does not work for either one.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
For the verse says:
"Do not take a woman to her sister, to make them rivals,"

phrases.aramaic: הַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ צָרוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ,
phrases.english: The Torah said: at the moment they would become rival wives to each other,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא לוֹ לִיקּוּחִים אֲפִילּוּ בְּאַחַת מֵהֶם.
phrases.english: he will not have a taking even with one of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק's word לצרור teaches that קידושין which would make sisters rivals at once fails for both.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the punishment of כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if this פסוק means קידושין doesn't take effect, how does the later פסוק give כרת for this sin?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, what about what is written: "the souls that do them shall be cut off from among their people"? If קידושין doesn't take hold on her, is he liable for כרת?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רמי בר חמא's reading of the פסוק. He points to the punishment of כרת listed for these sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives כרת for being with a wife's sister. That only makes sense if the first sister is really his wife. If רמי בר חמא is right that this פסוק is about קידושין not working, then it is hard to see where the כרת comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off, a heavenly punishment

phrases.english: Rava said to him: If so,
what about that which is written:
"the souls that do them shall be cut off from among their people"?
If קידושין doesn't take hold on her,
is he liable for כרת?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רמי בר חמא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's reading that the פסוק of לצרור is about קידושין failing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The section of the Torah gives כרת for these sins, which needs a valid marriage. That does not fit a reading where this פסוק is about קידושין not working.

steps.title: רבא's answer: the פסוק is about one after the other, and the simultaneous case follows רבה's rule
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the פסוק about two sisters speaks about taking them one after the other, where כרת applies. The ruling that simultaneous קידושין fails comes from רבה's principle: what cannot work one after the other cannot work at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The פסוק is talking about one after the other. The משנה follows רבה, who said: anything that cannot take effect one after the other cannot take effect even at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 23's challenge knocked out רמי בר חמא's source, so רבא offers his own answer to the question 'from where do we know this?' The פסוק is about marrying sisters one after the other, and the case of 'both at once' gets its rule from a logical principle of רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא used the פסוק itself to teach that simultaneous קידושין fails, but then the פסוק could not also be the source of כרת. רבא splits the two jobs. The פסוק handles the one-after-the-other case: the second sister is forbidden, so living with her brings כרת. The 'at the same time' case is solved by רבה's rule: since he could never have both one after the other, he cannot get both at once either, so neither is betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier approach is being set aside for a new one.

steps.confusionAlert: רָבָא and רַבָּה are two different אמוראים with very similar names. Here רבא is the one answering, and he relies on a rule said by רבה.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבה's principle becomes a general rule that the גמרא now tests on its own, far beyond the case of sisters.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava says:
The verse is about one after the other,
and the משנה follows Rabba.
phrases.notes: This is the teaching from step 19: a woman and her sister betrothed at the same moment.

phrases.english: As Rabba says:
Anything that cannot take effect one after the other
cannot take effect even at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבא's challenge from step 23 by replacing רמי בר חמא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning sources: the פסוק covers the sequential case, and a logical principle covers the simultaneous case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק itself teaches that simultaneous קידושין of sisters fails, which makes the כרת פסוק hard to explain.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is about one sister after the other, which is where כרת applies. Simultaneous קידושין fails because of רבה's rule that what cannot work one after the other cannot work at once.

steps.title: Looking at רבה's rule on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats רבה's principle so it can examine it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the matter itself: רבה said, anything that cannot take effect one after the other cannot take effect even at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the main discussion and quotes רבה's rule again so it can study that rule by itself. This is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to a statement it just mentioned in passing, to look at it closely. The rule is repeated word for word, now as the main topic instead of as a support for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself'. The גמרא returns to examine a statement it quoted in passing.

phrases.english: Now the matter itself.
Rabba says:
Anything that cannot take effect one after the other
cannot take effect even at the same time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the principle quoted in step 24 and makes it the subject of its own discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that cannot take effect one after the other cannot take effect even at the same time.

steps.title: אביי begins a challenge to רבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי raises an objection to רבה's principle. The source he uses comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised an objection to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only opens a challenge. אביי is about to quote a source that seems to go against רבה's rule, and that source comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word איתיביה means a challenge from an earlier source, usually a ברייתא. Here we only see the opening formula. The actual problem for רבה's rule will appear in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him, usually by quoting a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' means רבה. The source אביי quotes comes right after this line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the principle just restated in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's principle that what cannot take effect one after the other cannot take effect at the same time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source that comes next will apparently show something that works at the same time even though it would not work one after the other.
